text:
The abstract directly reports that a set of contextual determinants—spanning organizational (e.g., collaboration between provider organizations, fee‑for‑service plans), community (e.g., school‑based health centers, urban residence, regional residence, area socioeconomic status, mental‑health care accessibility), and public‑policy factors (e.g., mental‑health parity laws, screening programs, health‑insurance extensions)—are positively associated with children’s and adolescents’ mental‑health care utilization. This aligns precisely with Hypothesis 2, while the other hypotheses introduce additional constructs or mechanisms that are not addressed in the study.

CHOICE: 2
